::: gc-box
My research sits at the crossroads of **plant pathology**, **molecular biology** and **crop genetics**.
The big question: *how can we make lettuce tougher against fungi that kill first and eat later?*
:::

## &#129440; Necrotrophic fungi

*Botrytis cinerea* (grey mould) and *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum* (white mould) are broad host-range
necrotrophs that cause huge losses in lettuce and many other crops. I study the host side of
these interactions &mdash; which genes and pathways help the plant resist.

## &#129516; Transcription factors in defence <span class="new">NEW!</span>

One of my projects looks at **LsERF1**, a lettuce ERF-family transcription factor, by
overexpressing it in *Arabidopsis* and testing what it does to disease resistance.
*(Paper in preparation &mdash; watch this space!)*

## &#9986;&#65039; Genome editing & omics

CRISPR-based editing and omics approaches to find and test resistance genes in
*Lactuca sativa* and its wild relatives.

## &#127757; Wild *Lactuca* of Türkiye

Türkiye is home to many wild lettuce relatives &mdash; a treasure chest of
resistance diversity waiting to be explored.
